identity.title: Observed CN and HCN intensity ratios exhibit subtle variations in extreme galaxy environments
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We use both new and archival ALMA data of three energy lines each of CN and HCN to explore intensity ratios in dense gas in NGC 3256, NGC 7469, and IRAS 13120-5453.

In this paper, we present the results of an observational study of the intensity ratios of CN and HCN in three U/LIRGs. We use both new and archival ALMA observations of three lines each of CN and HCN.

findings_qualitative.value: HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) varies spatially within NGC 3256 and NGC 7469 with superlinear trends, peaking in the nuclei, whereas IRAS 13120 shows higher overall ratios (~0.8) with little spatial variation at ~700 pc resolution.

evidence.quote: The HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) intensity ratio varies in NGC 3256 and NGC 7469, with superlinear trends of $1.53\pm0.07$ and $1.55\pm0.05$, respectively.
At our resolution ($\sim700$ pc), IRAS 13120-5453 shows little variation in the HCN intensity ratios.

findings_qualitative.value: Individual galaxies exhibit nearly constant CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) intensity ratios, with NGC 3256 offset to lower values (~0.45) compared to NGC 7469 and IRAS 13120 (~0.8).

evidence.quote: We find relatively constant CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) ratios and subtle variations in the CN (3-2)/CN (2-1) ratio in our galaxy sample. We find an offset to lower ratios of $\sim0.45$ in the CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) ratio in NGC 3256 compared to $\sim0.8$ in NGC 7469 and IRAS 13120.

findings_qualitative.value: Enhanced CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) ratios (~1.7) are found in strong starburst regions (IRAS 13120 and the northern nucleus of NGC 3256), whereas the AGN-dominated galaxy NGC 7469 shows a constant lower ratio (~1.1).

evidence.quote: We find high ($\sim1.7$) CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) intensity ratios in IRAS 13120-5453 and in the northern nucleus of NGC 3256, compared to a more constant ratio ($\sim1.1$) in NGC 7469 and non-starbursting regions of NGC 3256.

claims.hypothesis: HCN excitation is enhanced in regions of strong starburst and/or AGN activity in U/LIRGs.
claims.experiment: Measure spatially resolved HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) and HCN (4-3)/HCN (3-2) intensity ratios and pixel-by-pixel log-log slopes across nuclear and non-nuclear regions of NGC 3256, NGC 7469, and IRAS 13120.
claims.result: HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) shows superlinear slopes of 1.53+/-0.07 (NGC 3256) and 1.55+/-0.05 (NGC 7469), rising from 0.33+/-0.04 (non-nuclear) to 0.52+/-0.06 (nuclear) in NGC 7469, and reaching 0.80+/-0.09 globally in IRAS 13120.
claims.finding: HCN excitation is enhanced in the nuclei of NGC 3256 and NGC 7469 and globally in IRAS 13120 due to AGN XDR/outflow heating and high star formation rate surface densities.

evidence.quote: The HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) ratio in NGC 7469 shows the largest difference between non-nuclear ($0.33\pm0.04$) and nuclear ($0.52\pm0.06$) regions. We attribute the regions of enhanced HCN excitation in NGC 7469 to the central AGN, where both an XDR and shocks in outflows can heat the gas and increase HCN excitation.
The HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) ratio in IRAS 13120 is higher ($\sim0.8$) than both NGC 3256 ($\sim0.27-0.39$) and NGC 7469 ($\sim0.33-0.52$).

claims.hypothesis: CN excitation varies across extreme galaxy environments in response to AGN and starburst radiation fields.
claims.experiment: Measure CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) and CN (3-2)/CN (2-1) intensity ratios and pixel-by-pixel slopes across the three galaxies.
claims.result: CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) slopes are nearly constant (~0.93+/-0.05) within each galaxy, with NGC 3256 offset to ~0.45 versus ~0.8 in NGC 7469 and IRAS 13120; CN (3-2)/CN (2-1) shows superlinear slopes, peaking at 1.55+/-0.04 in NGC 7469 (0.45+/-0.06 in the nucleus vs 0.30+/-0.04 non-nuclear).
claims.finding: CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) is largely constant within individual galaxies, while higher-excitation CN (3-2)/CN (2-1) is locally enhanced by the nuclear AGN and circumnuclear environment in NGC 7469 and globally high in IRAS 13120.

evidence.quote: Individual galaxies show nearly constant CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) intensity ratios. We find an offset to lower CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) intensity ratios ($\sim0.5$) in NGC 3256 compared to the other two galaxies ($\sim0.8$).
For the CN (3-2)/CN (2-1) intensity ratio, NGC 7469 has a superlinear trend of $1.55\pm0.04$, with the peak localized toward the active galactic nucleus.

claims.hypothesis: The CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) intensity ratio increases in regions exposed to intense UV and X-ray radiation fields.
claims.experiment: Compare spatially resolved CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) intensity ratios across starburst-dominated regions (IRAS 13120, NGC 3256 northern nucleus) and AGN-dominated regions (NGC 7469 nucleus, NGC 3256 southern nucleus), and model column densities with RADEX.
claims.result: CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) is 1.7+/-0.1 in IRAS 13120 and the NGC 3256 northern nucleus (corresponding to N_CN/N_HCN ~ 24 in RADEX vs ~ 10 in the disk), but remains constant at ~1.1 across NGC 7469 and the rest of NGC 3256.
claims.finding: Intense starburst UV radiation fields enhance the CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) intensity ratio, whereas the nuclear AGN and XDR in NGC 7469 do not affect the ratio as significantly at ~300 pc resolution.

evidence.quote: The CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) ratio is higher ($1.7$) in the northern nucleus of NGC 3256 than in the rest of the galaxy. We find a similarly high CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) ratio in the starburst galaxy IRAS 13120.

The CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) ratio in NGC 7469 is $\sim1.1$ and is relatively constant across the entire galaxy. NGC 7469 is dominated by a nuclear AGN, which does not appear to affect the CN/HCN ratio as significantly as the starbursts in the other galaxies.

why_this_data.value: Three U/LIRGs hosting different combinations of starbursts and AGN observed in three transitions each of CN and HCN allow probing the effects of both UV (PDR) and X-ray (XDR) radiation fields on dense gas excitation at spatial scales isolating nuclear and disk regions.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we present the results of an observational study of the intensity ratios of CN and HCN in three U/LIRGs. We use both new and archival ALMA observations of three lines each of CN and HCN. The higher energy lines allow us to explore the interaction between these molecules in a variety of radiation environments.
The different galaxy environments available in this sample allow us to probe the effects of both UV and X-ray radiation fields on the molecular gas.

why_this_method.value: Matching uv ranges, channel widths, and beams across all 6 lines per galaxy ensures recovery of similar spatial scales; masking at 3.5 sigma across all 6 lines avoids noisy emission; Linmix accounts for larger uncertainties in lower S/N pixels during log-log fitting.

evidence.quote: The UVRANGE parameter was matched between all lines in each galaxy in order to recover similar flux scales for each line.
An RMS cut-off of $3.5\sigma$ was used to mask the cleaned cubes to include strong emission while avoiding noisy emission in lines with lower S/N.

We used the Linmix linear regression method to fit the integrated intensity pixels in log-log space and account for the higher uncertainties seen in the lower S/N pixels (cite: Kelly2007; Meyers2018).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Applying an inclination angle correction of 60 degrees to NGC 3256 and IRAS 13120 was tested, but omitted because NGC 3256 has two nuclei with different inclinations, IRAS 13120 has no literature inclination, and the resulting slopes and intercepts matched the uncorrected ones within 1 sigma.

evidence.quote: We performed the same analysis applying a conservative estimate for inclination angles of $60^\circ$ to NGC 3256 and IRAS 1320 and found that the resulting slopes and intercepts match the results in Table 5 within one standard deviation.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Requiring a 93 GHz radio continuum detection in each pixel (used by Wilson et al. in prep.) was not adopted so that the analysis could extend to lower line intensities.

evidence.loc: The CN/HCN intensity ratio as a probe of radiation field
evidence.quote: Since we are not requiring 93 GHz continuum detections, we can extend our analysis to the lower line intensities where we find most of our variations in the CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) ratios.

limitations_admitted.value: Applying UVRANGE cut-offs and UVTAPER in TCLEAN limits short baselines and can lead to missing flux on the largest angular scales.

evidence.quote: We note that applying a *uv* cut-off and taper with the UVRANGE and UVTAPER parameters in TCLEAN will limit the number of short baselines in our data and thus could potentially lead to missing flux on the largest angular scales.

limitations_admitted.value: Spatial resolutions (~300 pc in NGC 7469, ~470 pc in NGC 3256, ~700 pc in IRAS 13120) do not resolve individual XDRs (<50 pc) and blend AGN, starburst, and outflow shock contributions within the central beam.

evidence.loc: Increased nuclear HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) ratio in NGC 7469
evidence.quote: Our observations of NGC 7469 have a resolution of $\sim300$ pc and thus blend the influence of both AGN and starburst activity in the circumnuclear disk.

evidence.loc: Higher HCN (3-2)/HCN (1-0) ratios in IRAS 13120 than NGC 3256
evidence.quote: Our resolution of $\sim700$ pc is insufficient to isolate the nuclear region and so the line ratio will have contributions from both the starburst and AGN components in this galaxy.

limitations_admitted.value: The CN (1-0) dataset for NGC 3256 is from ALMA Cycle 0 and has high calibration uncertainties, meaning the offset to lower CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) ratios in NGC 3256 could be an observational artifact.

evidence.quote: The CN (1-0) data for NGC 3256 is our only data set from ALMA Cycle 0. As such, the flux measurements and intensity ratios using this line in this galaxy have the highest calibration uncertainties of our sample. Given the similarity of the slopes in the CN (2-1)/CN (1-0) ratio of all three galaxies, the offset in the ratio in NGC 3256 could be due to large observational uncertainties.

limitations_admitted.value: Observed integrated intensity ratios are affected by gas temperature, density, and optical depth (opacity) effects, so full non-LTE radiative transfer modelling is required to determine true molecular abundance ratios.

evidence.quote: We note that opacity effects could potentially be important and determining the CN/HCN abundance ratios is the next step in this analysis.

referee_caveats_inferred: Physical spatial resolutions differ by more than a factor of 2 across the sample (304 pc in NGC 7469 vs 715 pc in IRAS 13120), making direct comparisons of nuclear versus global ratios sensitive to beam dilution.
In Section 2.2.2 (NGC 7469 processing), CN (3-2) is listed under both robust = 0.5 and natural weighting while CN (2-1) is omitted, creating a minor ambiguity in the exact imaging recipe.

data_public_as_stated.value: Public data available in the ALMA archive under the project IDs in Table 2; processed data cubes available from the authors by request.

evidence.quote: This research is based on public data available in the ALMA archive and the exact project IDs can be found in Table [\[tab:Project_IDs\]](#tab:Project_IDs). The whole dataset and processed data cubes can be obtained from the authors by request.

missing_for_reproduction: Exact UVTAPER parameters per line and galaxy in TCLEAN
Velocity integration windows (Table B1 / tab:imaging_vel_props referenced as being in the Appendix, which is not included in the provided text)
Full slope and intercept table (Table B3 / tab:slopes_full) and full measured ratio table (tab:measured_ratios_full) from the Appendix
Resolution of the typo in Section 2.2.2 regarding whether CN (2-1) or CN (3-2) used robust = 0.5 vs natural weighting in NGC 7469
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~100-300 GB of raw visibility data across 11 ALMA projects (18 galaxy-line combinations); a few GB for the reduced and smoothed spectral cubes.
reproducibility.score_reason: All 11 ALMA project codes are explicitly tabulated, CASA version (5.6.1), UVRANGE cut-offs, pixel sizes, channel widths, target beam sizes, masking thresholds (2 sigma cleaning, 3.5 sigma moment 0), and regression software (Linmix) are clearly specified. Minor deductions for omitted exact UVTAPER values, a typo in NGC 7469 weighting, and velocity integration windows being in an omitted appendix.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: All raw ALMA data are public in the archive with exact project IDs provided, the uv-matching, imaging, and moment-0 masking procedures are well-defined, and the primary results are quantitative regional intensity ratios and log-log regression slopes.

methods_papers.why: AUTO-MULTITHRESH algorithm in CASA TCLEAN used for automated masking during deconvolution
Bayesian linear regression method and Python package (Linmix) used to fit pixel-by-pixel intensities in log-log space
RADEX non-LTE radiative transfer code used to estimate CN/HCN column density ratios

companion_papers.why: Companion ALMA study analysing global CN (1-0)/HCN (1-0) intensity ratios and 93 GHz continuum across 9 galaxies including NGC 3256, NGC 7469, and IRAS 13120
